headline: Workflows and databases convert genome and amplicon sequences into taxonomic and functional assignments
label: Sequence Based Taxonomic Workflows
summary: New pipelines and an updated mOTUs database make species assignment, 16S profiling and genome alignment more reproducible and accessible.
synthesis: The dominant thread is tooling that turns raw nucleotide sequence into taxonomic, comparative or functional annotations, with an emphasis on reproducible, accessible workflows. Robust Cluster Typing uses ribosomal proteins in a Snakemake/Python workflow to assign bacterial genomes to species-level clusters, demonstrated on Campylobacter. VPHYL converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore abundance tables into phyloseq or BIOM objects. nf-core/pairgenomealign packages pairwise whole-genome alignment with LAST as a Nextflow pipeline with benchmarking. The updated mOTUs database links taxonomy with genome-encoded function and biogeography, with a CLI and API. These items differ in scope, from species designation to alignment and profiling resources, and the summaries do not support cross-tool performance comparisons.
